hard_invariants: Preparation uncertainty and measurement error-disturbance are not treated as the same theorem.
Decoherence and readout noise are modeled separately from intrinsic incompatibility.
Quantum error correction is not described as removing noncommutation.
No observed hardware result is invented.

selected_primary_idea.title: Uncertainty Budget Tomography: Calibrated Separation of Incompatibility, Instrument Disturbance, Decoherence, and Readout Noise
selected_primary_idea.abstract: A qubit-focused protocol that jointly calibrates state preparation, a generalized measurement instrument, an open-system channel, and classical readout, then tests whether the resulting decomposition improves prediction of an entropic or state-prediction task.
selected_primary_idea.scientific_object: A single qubit, with an optional correlated ancilla or memory qubit, measured in deliberately incompatible bases.
selected_primary_idea.mechanism: Noncommutation constrains preparation spreads; the apparatus, channel, and readout map those intrinsic distributions to observed records through distinct, calibratable transformations.
selected_primary_idea.intervention: Vary basis angle, input Bloch vector, generalized-measurement strength, channel parameter, readout confusion matrix, and optional memory correlation while holding the analysis contract fixed.
selected_primary_idea.validation_protocol: Compare a preregistered four-term model against an aggregate-noise baseline on held-out qubit settings, with calibration ablations and uncertainty propagation.
falsifiers: The four terms are not identifiable from the declared preparation, instrument, channel, and readout calibration data.
The UBT model does not improve held-out prediction of the selected information metric relative to the aggregate-noise baseline.
Independently calibrated channel or measurement data disagree with the inferred decomposition outside stated uncertainty intervals.
claim_boundaries: The project does not claim that uncertainty can be eliminated.
The project does not treat every environmental interaction as an instantaneous projective collapse.
The project does not interpret quantum error correction as defeating noncommutation.

competitive_ideas.title: Calibrated entropic uncertainty with quantum memory

high_risk_ideas.title: Cross-platform uncertainty budget transfer between photonic and spin-compatible models

rejected_ideas.title: Use quantum error correction to remove quantum uncertainty
rejected_ideas.reason: Violates the Survey invariant separating mitigation of noise from noncommutation.

rejected_ideas.title: Treat all observed randomness as decoherence
rejected_ideas.reason: Collapses preparation uncertainty, instrument effects, and readout noise into one unsupported category.

mcts_evolution_summary.result: Separated preparation uncertainty from device-level noise and disturbance.
Combined calibrated instrument and channel models with entropic task metrics.
Selected a held-out predictive comparison rather than a narrative-only interpretation.
